subject.title: Create Claw agent and root install record

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this experimental core `claws add` lifecycle—agent/workspace mutation plus durable ownership provenance—as an accepted staged direction before reviewing this implementation for landing?
rationale: The branch is not a narrow bug fix: it creates a new persistent core lifecycle, public consent flags, and future ownership semantics shared with downstream status/remove work. Code review cannot determine whether that product and ownership boundary belongs in core.

options.title: Sponsor the staged core lifecycle
options.body: Accept the Claws direction, land the prerequisite planning slice first, then require a current-head mutation/retry proof before merging this slice.

options.title: Keep Claws preview-only
options.body: Retain the existing read-only planning direction and close or redesign the mutating lifecycle outside core until a future approved proposal exists.

options.title: Narrow the scope first
options.body: Request a smaller approved core seam that defers persistent ownership and agent creation until lifecycle ownership is settled.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the staged core lifecycle
recommendation.body: Accept the Claws direction, land the prerequisite planning slice first, then require a current-head mutation/retry proof before merging this slice.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline identifies this person as an explicitly notified stakeholder, and the outstanding question is product direction rather than a mechanical patch repair.
